traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied.
• Core Functionality: The rule visits significant branch node types (if, switch case, try/catch/finally, for/while/do-while, for-in/of) and, via `reportMissingAnnotations`, detects when @story and/or @req annotations are absent. Multiple invalid test cases verify detection and the exact error messages.
• Quality Standards: Implementation follows ESLint best practices (RuleModule with meta/docs/schema/messages, RuleTester tests, separation into helper utilities). The logic is linear in branch count and uses simple regex and array operations, appropriate for large files.
• Integration: `require-branch-annotation` is included in the plugin’s exported rule set and in both `recommended` and `strict` configs as an error, so it participates in normal lint workflows. The flat ESLint config is set up to load the plugin from src/lib.
• User Experience: Error messages are clear and specific: `Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.`, with `missing` bound to `@story` or `@req`. Auto-fix behavior adds placeholder annotations (`// @story .story.md` and `// @req `), demonstrated and asserted in tests.
• Error Handling: Invalid `branchTypes` configuration triggers a dedicated Program listener that reports a clear configuration error for each invalid type, rather than crashing. Special handling for `SwitchCase` default branches and comment scanning around cases prevents false positives and handles tricky layouts.
• Documentation: The rule has its own documentation file linked to this story, showing configuration (`branchTypes`), valid/invalid code examples, and invalid configuration behavior. Implementation and tests are fully annotated with @story and @req tags referencing this story, maintaining traceability.
Nested branches are handled naturally by ESLint’s traversal (listeners are attached to node types regardless of depth), and the overall design is efficient, satisfying the nested-handling and performance-related requirements. Therefore this story is fully implemented and passes.
